title: Adaptive kernel selection + prefill-decode overlap to reduce tail latency
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Prefill and decode stages historically execute mostly serially which leaves GPU kernels underutilized at certain request size/latency envelopes. This PR implements an adaptive runtime strategy to overlap chunked prefill work with early decode steps while leveraging a dynamic kernel selection policy that favors low-latency kernels for short sequences and high-throughput kernels for long-running decodes. The goal is to reduce p95/p99 end-to-end latency and improve throughput at moderate concurrency without changing the public API.

Design summary: three complementary components are introduced: 1) Prefill chunking and speculative overlap: requests with long prefill context are split into configurable chunks (runtime.prefill_chunk_size) and the scheduler permits decoding to start on earlier chunks once a safe KV state is available. A speculation controller estimates token-lag and decides when to start decode lanes. 2) Adaptive kernel selector: a new kernel policy layer (runtime.kernel_policy) picks per-stage kernels based on observed sequence length distribution, current occupancy, and a short MA window of latency metrics. This allows using lower-latency attention kernels on short decode runs while switching to throughput-optimized kernels for long prefill-heavy requests. 3) KV cache pre-warm and consistency fences: to support overlap we add lightweight KV pre-warm hooks and sequence-consistency fences to ensure decode reads are correct when prefill is still producing trailing KV updates. These fences are fine-grained and avoid global stalls.

Config and flags: runtime.enable_prefill_overlap=true (opt-in), runtime.prefill_chunk_size=64 (default), runtime.speculative_prefill=true, runtime.kernel_policy=dynamic. All flags are runtime-configurable and can be toggled per-deployment.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on r4-highmem (A100-equivalent) using internal genbench harness. Representative results vs main: - 512-token average requests at 16 concurrent streams: p95 latency -12.5%, p99 latency -18.7%, aggregate throughput +9%. - 2048-token prefill-heavy workloads: throughput +14% due to better kernel throughput switching. Impact on memory: typical KV working set memory increased by ~2-4% due to chunking metadata, validated within budget for Dedicated nodes.

Compatibility and safety: feature gated behind runtime.enable_prefill_overlap. When disabled, behavior identical to main. Extensive correctness tests added to ensure kv-cache invariants under speculative overlap.

Testing and rollout: unit tests, integration tests with simulated interleaving of prefill/decode, and end-to-end smoke tests included. Gradual rollout plan via canary on Dedicated pools with a fallback policy to revert to non-overlapping execution if any tail latency regression is observed.

Notes: This work touches hot path scheduling and kernel selection; storage-layer and multi-tenant implications are handled conservatively. Further followups will explore cross-request prefix caching and more aggressive speculative decode heuristics.
commit_summary: 6 commits: initial adaptive-kernel-layer; add prefill chunking scheduler; KV pre-warm and fences; spec controller + heuristics; tests and benchmarks; docs and toggles
review_comments: Ethan Zhou: Nice clean split of scheduler. Two asks: (1) add a memory pressure fallback so chunking backs off under OOM risk, (2) add more unit tests around fence edge-cases.
Maya Patel: Added memory-pressure heuristic and three additional unit tests in prefill_overlap_test.cpp; clarified doc on fence semantics.
Priya Nair: Found a race condition on worker shutdown where a fence waiter could be dropped. Please ensure joins or cancellation signal are handled.
Maya Patel: Fixed shutdown join ordering and added test that asserts no outstanding fence waiters after cancel; CI re-run.
Liam O'Connor: Benchmarks look good. Could you include p99 throughput curves in the docs? Also OOM risk note for smaller GPUs.
Maya Patel: Added p99 curve images and a short note about prefill_chunk_size tuning for 16GB GPUs in docs.
release_notes: runtime: add opt-in adaptive prefill-decode overlap and dynamic kernel selection. Reduces tail latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads; opt-in via runtime.enable_prefill_overlap. See docs/runtime/prefill_overlap.md for tuning guidance.
notes_for_qa: QA should exercise: 1) long prefill (>1024 tokens) requests with overlap enabled/disabled, 2) shutdown/worker restart during overlapping prefill/decode, 3) memory-constrained nodes (16GB) to validate prefill_chunk_size tuning, 4) multi-tenant noise injection to ensure no cache cross-talk.

Monitor p99 latency dashboards for prefixed routes
